AK.key_factor: Peltola leads October first-choice polls by about three points, but Republican-leaning transfers from Heikes and the same-name Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. should narrow that edge in the ranked-choice count.
AK.reasoning: Peltola took 49.5% in the August primary, leads most October polls and has a 2.6-to-1 money edge in a D+8 national climate. Second choices from Heikes and Sullivan Jr. voters should favor Sullivan, though. Alaska polls overstated Democrats in 2020, and the Oct 28 spoiler-recruitment report and the state and federal investigations land in the final week. A coin flip with a slight Peltola lean; shares are first-choice.

FL.key_factor: Moody leads October polls by about six points in a state whose polls have understated Republicans in every cycle since 2018.
FL.reasoning: Every October poll shows Moody ahead, by 2 to 12 points, and Florida polls missed toward Democrats by several points in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024. The D+8 national climate, a near-even partisan early vote and heavy Democratic outside spending should narrow Rubio's 16-point 2022 margin. Florida's R+13 lean and Nixon's DSA-aligned platform, which limits crossover appeal, still leave Moody comfortably favored.

IA.key_factor: The race is tied in polling, and Iowa polls have understated Republicans by several points in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024.
IA.reasoning: Nonpartisan polls average roughly a tie, and Republican-sponsored polls lean Hinson by 1 to 2 points. Turek has a large money edge, and an open governor's race plus the D+8 climate help Democratic turnout. Iowa's R+13 lean and its persistent pro-Democratic polling error still favor Hinson modestly. Libertarian Laehn should take 2 to 3%, mostly from the right, which keeps the margin tight.

KS.key_factor: Since Trump's Oct 20 rally defending Marshall's lawsuits against patients, independent polls show Hamilton ahead by 3 to 9 points.
KS.reasoning: The race was roughly tied through mid-October; since then Emerson, CNN/SSRS and the Washington Post have found Hamilton +3 to +9. Marshall ran three points behind Trump in 2020, the patient-arrest story is personal and sticky, and Hamilton has outraised him 2.5-to-1. Kansas federal-race polls overstated Democrats badly in 2014 and 2020, the state is R+16, and late Republican money is arriving, so Hamilton's edge is thin.

ME.key_factor: Jackson leads most October polls by 2 to 4 points, and Collins can overcome that only if she again beats her polls as she did in 2020.
ME.reasoning: Recent polls average about Jackson +2.5, and the trend moved his way in October. A D+7 state in a D+8 midterm under an unpopular Republican president is hostile ground, and Jackson's rural, labor profile competes for Collins's northern base. Collins beat her final 2020 polls by double digits on the margin, so I discount Jackson's lead heavily. That leaves a near coin flip that tilts Jackson.

MI.key_factor: El-Sayed leads nearly every October poll, by about five points in the final two weeks, in a state the D+8 environment pushes well left of its 2024 result.
MI.reasoning: Late polls from SSRS, Mitchell, Glengariff, MSU and even Rasmussen show El-Sayed up 5 to 8. Michigan was only R+1.4 in 2024, so this national climate makes it lean Democratic. The margin stays modest because Rogers is well known after nearly winning in 2024, has $35 million in outside help, and AIPAC-linked attacks are targeting El-Sayed's progressive record.

MN.key_factor: Flanagan leads every October poll, including Republican-sponsored ones, in a D+4 state during a D+8 national environment.
MN.reasoning: October polls range from Flanagan +3 in Republican surveys to +14 in Siena, averaging about +6. Undecided voters are likely to break toward the DFL in this climate. Trump's endorsement of Tafoya probably hurts more than it helps in Minnesota, and the state's polls have been reasonably accurate in recent cycles. The independent and Libertarian candidates should take about 3%.

NC.key_factor: Cooper leads every poll, by about 10 points in nonpartisan surveys, and registered Democrats outnumber Republicans 925,000 to 604,000 in the early vote.
NC.reasoning: Even Republican pollsters show Cooper ahead by 5 to 10 points. The Senate Leadership Fund pulled $30 million from Whatley, and Cooper has outraised him nearly 4-to-1. The early-vote party mix is far more Democratic than in 2022 or 2024. North Carolina polls have tilted slightly toward Democrats in past cycles, but not by enough to erase a lead this size.

NE.key_factor: Polls show a near tie, but Nebraska polls overstated Osborn by several points against Fischer in 2024.
NE.reasoning: October surveys range from Osborn +7 to Ricketts +3, and Osborn's own internal poll shows Ricketts +2. The D+8 climate should help Osborn improve on his 6.7-point 2024 loss. Still, Nebraska is R+20, its undecided voters tend to come home to Republicans, and Osborn's 2024 polls overstated him. Expect a much closer race than 2024 that Ricketts narrowly holds.

NH.key_factor: Pappas has led every poll since mid-September by 5 to 8 points, including Republican-sponsored surveys.
NH.reasoning: Saint Anselm, UNH, Siena and YouGov all show Pappas up 5 to 8, and Republican pollsters find similar margins. A D+3 state in a D+8 midterm favors Democrats despite Sununu's famous family name. Pappas has outraised him about 4-to-1, though outside spending is roughly even. An upset would require a sizable statewide polling miss toward Republicans.

OH.key_factor: Brown leads independent polls by about four points, but Ohio polls have overstated Democrats by several points in every cycle since 2016.
OH.reasoning: Brown ran 7.6 points ahead of Harris in 2024, and a D+8 climate makes him competitive in an R+11 state. Independent polls show him up 3 to 6, while Republican pollsters show roughly a tie. After discounting Ohio's chronic pro-Democratic polling error, Brown keeps a narrow edge. A 3-to-1 fundraising advantage and the data-center backlash against Husted's tax-break record help him.

SC.key_factor: Graham leads nonpartisan polls by about two points in an R+18 state despite being a little-known, underfunded appointee.
SC.reasoning: Siena shows a tie, and other independent polls give Graham 1 to 4 points; South Carolina polls overstated Democrats from 2020 through 2024. Andrews has outraised Graham more than 10-to-1, and the D+8 climate plus Graham's thin record make this far closer than the 10-point 2020 race. The state's Republican floor is very high and its undecided voters usually come home, so Graham should hold narrowly.

TX.key_factor: Talarico leads late nonpartisan polls by about 2.5 points over a scandal-scarred Paxton, but Texas polls overstated Democrats in 2020, 2022 and 2024.
TX.reasoning: Polls fielded since mid-October average Talarico +2.6, and he has outraised Paxton more than 6-to-1 with a large outside-money edge. In the 2018 wave Texas polls underestimated O'Rourke, but from 2020 to 2024 they overstated Democrats by 2 to 6 points. The nearly 600,000-application registration backlog may also cost Talarico new voters. Net, a slight Talarico edge in a race that could easily go either way.

upset_watch.why: Peltola's narrow first-choice lead could vanish in the ranked-choice count, since Heikes and Sullivan Jr. ballots should transfer mostly to Sullivan just as the spoiler-recruitment scandal breaks.
